reasons.vendor:
NPX-893: boot timeout increased from 300 to 600s (Wave 21 U5 round 6: device was still reporting startup at 300s; needs more time to reach login prompt).
2026-09-06 retest (Wave 21 U5, node d10a44f7): 600s was STILL not enough - the
serial console produced literally zero bytes for the full window (opened
13:32:23, still silent at 13:39:56, host otherwise idle at load 6.4/40 cores -
ruled out host contention). Doubled to 1200s rather than guessing a smaller
bump, since 300->600 already proved once that this image's real boot time was
being underestimated.
reasons.config_dialect:
NPX-818 (Wave 21 U3): Cisco's SD-WAN (Viptela) boxes carry vendor "cisco", which
sent every one of them to VENDOR_CLI["cisco"] - IOS verbs. Viptela is not IOS: it
is a confd CLI whose configuration mode is entered with "config", committed with
"commit and-quit" and paged off with "paginate false", and whose "end"/"write
memory" equivalents do not exist. VENDOR_CLI already carries the correct
"viptela" dialect (authored and live-proved in an earlier wave); nothing ever
reached it, because a dialect is only selected by the vendor string unless a
profile names it. This is the same shape as NPX-617 (IOS-XR reached the IOS
dialect through vendor "cisco" and silently lost every config), so it is fixed
the same way and for the same reason.
reasons.emulator:
rule #59 (NPX-1527 profiles review, 2026-09-24): cpu_model aligned to EVE-NG's
vtedge.yml ("-cpu host") - no comment ever addressed this field.
reasons.nic:
e1000 is MANDATORY, not just this platform's generic-fallback default: virtio-net-pci
silently drops 802.1Q VLAN-tagged frames on vEdge's data-plane interfaces under
QEMU/KVM (docs/platform/node-emulation.md "Key SD-WAN Configuration Notes"). Pinning
it explicitly here so it stays correct even if GENERIC_KVM_PROFILE's own default
ever changes - it must never silently drift onto virtio-net-pci for this device.
